issues.description: Class name and message-format mismatch: The problem statement and template expect concrete classes named Goat, Pig, and Seal with methods that produce messages like "Goat [name] is milked" and "Riding on Pig [name]" (see problem statement tasks and UML). The solution repository, however, provides concrete implementations named SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal that produce messages prefixed with "Space" (e.g. "SpaceGoat Alice is milked"). Meanwhile the solution's Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java files are empty. This inconsistency between expected identifiers (Goat/Pig/Seal) and provided identifiers (SpaceGoat/SpacePig/SpaceSeal), plus the differing message text, will confuse students and test harnesses: students/readers will look for Goat/Pig/Seal implementations and the expected output strings, but the solution uses different class names and output formats.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifiers and expected output consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Add concrete Goat, Pig, and Seal classes to the solution repository that implement the required interfaces and constructors, and return messages exactly as specified in the problem (e.g. messageOnMilk() returns "Goat [name] is milked", messageOnRide() returns "Riding on Pig [name]"). Keep or remove the Space* classes as optional extras. Or: (B) If the intent is to use SpaceGoat/SpacePig/SpaceSeal, update the problem statement and template to reference these Space-prefixed class names and update expected message text accordingly. The preferred educational fix is (A) so students see the exact classes named in the tasks and matching output strings.

issues.description: The assignment and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (UML and task text call them Seal, Pig, Goat; the template's Main.java instantiates Seal, Pig, Goat), but the solution implementation provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead. This creates a direct identifier mismatch: the conceptual entities (seal, pig, goat) are represented by different class names in the solution. A student reading the problem and template will expect Seal, Pig, and Goat classes and may be unable to map the solution's SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat back to the required classes, which blocks comprehension and automated checks that rely on the expected identifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent between the problem/template and the solution. Rename the solution classes SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, and Goat (and update their constructors and any internal references) so they match the UML, task text, and the template Main.java. Alternatively, if the 'Space' prefix is intentional, update the problem statement and template to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat; the preferred fix is to rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat to match the assignment and reduce student confusion.
